principles: Only remove or wire code with a demonstrated correctness mismatch.
Keep current host-neutral Lattice workflow boundaries intact.
Prefer narrow product-tree cleanup over broad architecture rearrangement.
Preserve regression coverage for any behavior that remains supported.
drivers: The repo currently contains declared-but-unused dependency state and defined-but-unreachable implementation-review commands.
Package-local legacy active story metadata can confuse the active .lattice lifecycle model.
One-time migration scripts and legacy intent coverage helpers inflate the product tree unless clearly retained as supported tooling.

options.name: A: Minimal correctness cleanup and command wiring
pros: Fixes the concrete inconsistencies found by audit.
Keeps smoke tests and packages/lab out of scope.
Lowest behavioral risk while reducing misleading product surface.
cons: Leaves broader test/source layout cleanup for a future story.
Requires careful reference checks before deleting scripts or metadata.

options.name: B: Broad repository slimming pass
pros: Could reduce line count more aggressively.
Would make the tree look cleaner immediately.
cons: Risks deleting regression assets that protect Lattice lifecycle behavior.
Violates the no arbitrary optimization constraint.
Harder to verify as one focused correctness change.

options.name: C: Do nothing and document the debt
pros: Preserves all historical artifacts in place.
cons: Leaves unused dependency metadata and obsolete active-story residue visible in the product tree.
Does not satisfy the user-approved cleanup request.

chosen: A: Minimal correctness cleanup and command wiring
rationale: Choose the narrow cleanup because each target has a specific correctness or product-surface inconsistency, while broader slimming would optimize for appearance rather than real defects.

preMortem.scenario: A one-time migration script is still referenced by a test or doc example.
preMortem.trigger: Deletion happens before full rg/npm-script reference checks.
preMortem.consequence: Tests or documented maintenance workflows break silently.
preMortem.mitigation: Use rg and package script checks first; only delete scripts with no live product references or update obsolete docs in the same scoped change.

preMortem.scenario: implementation_review_result_set is wired without command schema or process fact alignment.
preMortem.consequence: The command exists but help, validation, or review process semantics drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Wire registry and command catalog together, add a focused smoke test that exercises help/set/get behavior.

preMortem.scenario: Removing intent-coverage.ts weakens legacy fixture compatibility unexpectedly.
preMortem.trigger: The file is deleted while fixtures still direct-import its dist module.
preMortem.consequence: Legacy fixture tests or coverage diagnostics fail after build.
preMortem.mitigation: Run reference checks and either remove/update direct legacy fixture tests or keep the module only if it has an active supported caller.

preMortem.scenario: Package-local old story metadata removal hides useful evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Deleting old docs/story files without confirming they are not used by runtime tests.
preMortem.consequence: Historical traceability or fixture expectations are lost.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep migrated .lattice evidence untouched and verify no live runtime references package-local active story files before deletion.
